questions.question: The Emotions' 'Best of My Love' — their 1977 #1 smash — was produced by which legendary leader of Earth, Wind & Fire?

metadata.fact: 'Best of My Love' spent five weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1977 — produced by Maurice White of Earth, Wind & Fire. The record brought the Hutchinson sisters to their commercial peak and stands as one of the era's most joyful love songs.
metadata.storyHook: Maurice White produced it. The Hutchinson sisters sang it. Five weeks at number one. 'Best of My Love' was 1977's purest shot of romantic soul.
metadata.sourceNotes: PRIORITY VERIFY: The Emotions 'Best of My Love' produced by Maurice White, #1 Hot 100 for 5 weeks (1977), Rejoice album. Must be sourced before production.

questions.question: Curtis Mayfield's 'Give Me Your Love (Love Song)' appeared on the soundtrack to which landmark 1972 blaxploitation film?

metadata.fact: Super Fly (1972) was Curtis Mayfield's soundtrack to the Gordon Parks Jr. film of the same name — and one of the defining albums of the blaxploitation era. 'Give Me Your Love (Love Song)' was the album's intimate centrepiece, providing a lush counterweight to the politically charged tracks surrounding it.
metadata.storyHook: The most romantic track on a politically charged soundtrack. Curtis Mayfield buried 'Give Me Your Love' inside Super Fly — and it became one of the album's most enduring moments.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Give Me Your Love (Love Song)' from Super Fly (1972), Curtom Records. questions.question: 'Love Ballad' was a 1976 R&B hit for which group — whose name stood for Love, Togetherness and Devotion?

metadata.fact: L.T.D. — Love, Togetherness and Devotion — released 'Love Ballad' from their 1976 album Love to the World on A&M Records. The group's lead vocalist was Jeffrey Osborne, whose powerful delivery on 'Love Ballad' established the template for the smooth, orchestrated R&B ballad that would define the late 70s and early 80s.
metadata.storyHook: Love, Togetherness and Devotion. The name said everything about the sound. L.T.D. and Jeffrey Osborne made 'Love Ballad' the era's definitive statement of romantic intent.

questions.question: 'Love Jones' was a 1972 soul hit recorded by which Chicago group — notable for featuring a lead singer who was just 13 years old?

metadata.fact: 'Love Jones' reached #16 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1972 and featured Darryl Lamont — just 13 years old — as the lead vocalist. The group formed around Chicago high school students, making 'Love Jones' one of the most unlikely crossover soul records of the decade.
metadata.storyHook: Thirteen years old. A Chicago high school group. A top-twenty soul hit. Brighter Side of Darkness made 'Love Jones' work against every expectation.

questions.question: Bobby Caldwell released 'What You Won't Do for Love' on which label — a TK Records subsidiary?

metadata.song: What You Won't Do for Love
topicTags: What You Won't Do for Love
metadata.fact: 'What You Won't Do for Love' was released on Cloud Records — a subsidiary of TK Records — in 1978. The label's strategy of keeping Bobby Caldwell's face off the album cover allowed the record to receive heavy airplay on Black radio stations without revealing that Caldwell was white, making it one of the more remarkable crossover stories of the decade.
metadata.storyHook: Cloud Records. A TK subsidiary. No face on the cover. Bobby Caldwell crossed over to Black radio in 1978 through a combination of talent and deliberate concealment.
metadata.sourceNotes: PRIORITY VERIFY: Bobby Caldwell 'What You Won't Do for Love' on Cloud Records (TK Records subsidiary), 1978, cover strategy. Must be sourced before production.

reserve.question: Rose Royce's 'Love Don't Live Here Anymore' was released on which label — founded by the producer who left Motown to build his own empire?

metadata.fact: 'Love Don't Live Here Anymore' was produced by Norman Whitfield — who had left Motown and founded Whitfield Records, releasing Rose Royce's records through that imprint. Whitfield's dense, dramatic production style — honed on Temptations records throughout the late 60s and early 70s — gave Rose Royce a cinematic grandeur that set them apart from contemporaries.

questions.question: Earth, Wind & Fire's 'Love's Holiday' appeared on which 1977 album — widely considered the peak of their classic period?
choices: That's the Way of the World

metadata.fact: All 'N All (1977) was Earth, Wind & Fire's seventh studio album and is widely regarded as the pinnacle of their classic period — featuring 'Love's Holiday,' 'September,' and 'Fantasy.' metadata.storyHook: All 'N All. 1977. 'Love's Holiday.' 'September.' 'Fantasy.' Earth, Wind & Fire put everything they had into one album — and it became their masterpiece.

questions.question: Before his solo career, Barry White first found fame as the lead voice behind which orchestral soul group?

reserve.question: Curtis Mayfield's Super Fly soundtrack was released on which label — his own imprint that gave him complete creative control?

metadata.fact: Curtom Records was Curtis Mayfield's own label — co-founded with Eddie Thomas in 1968 — giving him the creative autonomy that major label deals rarely permitted. The Super Fly soundtrack was released through Curtom, allowing Mayfield to make the politically complex, lyrically unflinching record he envisioned without commercial compromise.
metadata.storyHook: His own label. His own rules. Curtis Mayfield made the Super Fly soundtrack on Curtom Records — and nobody could tell him what it should sound like.

questions.question: Al Green — whose 'Love and Happiness' and 'I'm Still in Love with You' defined 70s romantic soul — was born under which full name?

metadata.fact: Al Green was born Albert Leornes Greene on April 13, 1946, in Forrest City, Arkansas. The name 'Al Green' — a professional simplification — gave nothing away about the extraordinary vocal instrument behind it.
metadata.storyHook: Albert Leornes Greene. Born in Forrest City, Arkansas. The name became Al Green. The voice became one of the great instruments of the 20th century.

questions.question: Jeffrey Osborne — the voice of L.T.D.'s 'Love Ballad' — was born in which US city?

metadata.fact: Jeffrey Osborne was born on March 9, 1948, in Providence, Rhode Island — one of the few major R&B artists of the era to emerge from New England. His powerful, emotionally direct tenor became the sonic identity of L.T.D. before his solo career confirmed him as one of the genre's most distinctive voices.
metadata.storyHook: Providence, Rhode Island. Not a city associated with 70s soul. But that's where the voice behind L.T.D.'s 'Love Ballad' came from.

reserve.question: The Emotions — the sisters who recorded 'Best of My Love' — all shared which surname?

metadata.fact: The Emotions were the Hutchinson sisters — Wanda, Sheila, and Jeanette — who grew up in Chicago and began singing together at their local church. Their gospel foundation gave 'Best of My Love' its joyful, almost ecstatic quality, and made them natural collaborators for Maurice White's similarly church-rooted production approach.
metadata.storyHook: Wanda, Sheila, and Jeanette Hutchinson. Three sisters. One church in Chicago. One number-one record. The Emotions made 'Best of My Love' sound like it cost nothing to feel.
